title: Sharp Connected-Interval Inference for Causal Expectile Contrasts at Two Reporting Atoms
banked_reason: The present fixed-benchmark kernel is coherent and not published-subsumed, but falls below the required field novelty tier; the clean class-wide extension emitted no typed core.
gap_reasons: The fixed public benchmark computes a new local decision value, but it neither supplies a matched minimax frontier nor a strict improvement/first bound for a named published estimator or causal estimand, so it remains a specialist letter-level benchmark rather than meeting the field novelty floor.
Every intervention reporting-category mass is at least 0.01.
The expectile contrast is 5/12, whereas the Gamma=1 comparator interval is [1/5,1/5].
Along h=(t,t), the difference observation has a fixed distribution while the contrast diverges, so coverage by any almost surely finite difference-only interval tends to zero.

An explicitly matched-slope compact subclass can avoid this obstruction, but unrestricted endpoint compactification, uniformly matched discretization, structural fiber certificates, and sharp uniform original-record attainment remain unresolved.
